title: J.Lo Tops the Chart in One Day: 'The JLO Show' Hits No. 1 on Paramount+ After Thanksgiving Premiere
excerpt: Jennifer Lopez's 'The JLO Show' hit No. 1 on Paramount+'s U.S. movie chart one day after its Thanksgiving premiere, powered by a Ja Rule reunion 25 years in the making.
content:
Jennifer Lopez needed exactly one day to top the streaming chart. The JLO Show, her new concert film, premiered on CBS and Paramount+ on Thanksgiving night and reached No. 1 on Paramount+'s U.S. movie chart the following day, November 27, according to FlixPatrol — and it was still holding the top spot on Saturday.

The two-hour special was filmed on March 28, 2026, the closing night of Lopez's Las Vegas residency, Jennifer Lopez: Up All Night Live in Las Vegas, at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace. The residency ran 12 shows from December 30, 2025, to March 28, 2026.

A Bronx-to-Vegas retrospective in five acts

The film traces Lopez's journey from the Bronx to global stardom across five acts, blending her biggest pop hits with personal storytelling and tributes to the entertainers who shaped Las Vegas. Backed by a full orchestra, a vocal ensemble and 16 dancers, she performs “Jenny from the Block,” “Waiting for Tonight,” “Love Don’t Cost a Thing,” “Get Right” and “Let’s Get Loud,” alongside Broadway numbers including “Let Me Entertain You” and “Don’t Rain on My Parade,” and covers of Elvis Presley’s “Heartbreak Hotel” and Lana Del Rey’s “Young and Beautiful.”

The show also salutes Chita Rivera, Marilyn Monroe and Barbra Streisand, and includes the title number from Kiss of the Spider Woman.

The reunion fans waited 25 years to see

The most talked-about moment is the reunion with Ja Rule. The rapper joined Lopez onstage for “I’m Real” and “Ain’t It Funny,” the two early-2000s collaborations that defined their run together. The Murder Remix of “I’m Real” reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2001, and the “Ain’t It Funny” remix did the same in 2002.

The special aired at 8 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving, November 26, on CBS and Paramount+, with an extended version streaming exclusively on Paramount+. The CBS broadcast carried a shorter cut; the full two-hour version is the streaming exclusive.

Analysis: why a concert film won Thanksgiving night

The timing was deliberate counterprogramming. The special aired 20 minutes before the Kansas City Chiefs–Buffalo Bills game kicked off, offering a music event for viewers who were not watching football — and the nostalgia at its center did the heavy lifting. Concert films have become reliable streaming events, and Lopez paired a career retrospective with the one reunion her audience had waited a quarter-century to see again.

The chart result is the early verdict: a one-day climb to No. 1, with the film still topping the U.S. chart on Saturday and reaching No. 1 in Canada and Italy as well, according to FlixPatrol. Whether it holds through the weekend will show whether the Thanksgiving audience came for the reunion moment or stayed for the whole show.
